title: Remembering and sensing
about: Collocations for memory and the senses: a good memory, vaguely or vividly remember, memories come flooding back, blot out a memory, get the impression, trust your intuition, sensitive skin, go numb.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Якщо називаєш місце, де лишилася річ, краще кажи leave, а не forget: I left my notebook at home. Forget зазвичай уживають без місця: I've forgotten my notebook. І не плутай схожі слова: sensitive — вразливий, чутливий (a sensitive person — людина, яку легко образити), sensible — розсудливий (a sensible person — людина з тверезим судженням).

rows: I've forgotten my notebook at home.
I've left my notebook at home.

items.pattern: sb's long-term memory · in your long-term memory
items.meaning: your memory of things that happened a long time ago
items.example: Songs you learned as a child stay in your **long-term memory** for ever.
more: Revising a little every day helps new words go into your **long-term memory**.
Smells are closely linked to our **long-term memory**.
items.watchOut: «Довготривала пам'ять» — long-term memory, не long-time memory. A long memory — це інше: так кажуть про людину, яка довго пам'ятає образи (He has a long memory).

items.pattern: sb's short-term memory
items.meaning: your memory of things that happened very recently, a few minutes or hours ago
items.example: My **short-term memory** is so bad that I walk into the kitchen and forget why I came in.
more: Try to remember these ten words for one minute. It's a test of your **short-term memory**.
Stress can be bad for your **short-term memory**.

items.pattern: have a good / bad / terrible memory (for names / faces / numbers)
items.meaning: be good or bad at remembering things
items.example: My sister **has a really good memory** for birthdays: she never forgets anyone's.
more: I **have a terrible memory** for names, so I always write them down.
Dad used to **have a great memory**, but now he writes everything down.
items.watchOut: «Пам'ять на обличчя» — a good memory for faces, з for, не on. «У мене погана пам'ять» — I have a bad memory або My memory is terrible.

items.pattern: give sb a clue · Give me a clue! (informal)
items.meaning: tell someone a small piece of information to help them guess or remember something
items.example: I can't guess what's in the box. **Give me a clue**!
more: I'll **give you a clue**: it's red and you can eat it.
She couldn't remember my cousin's name, so I **gave her a clue**: it starts with M.
items.watchOut: «Підкажи» в сенсі «дай натяк» — give me a clue або give me a hint, не suggest me. А I haven't got a clue — «гадки не маю».

items.pattern: sb/sth reminds you (strongly) of sb/sth
items.meaning: be so similar to someone or something that you think of them
items.example: Your little boy **reminds me strongly of** my brother at that age.
more: The smell of pine trees always **reminds me of** our holidays in the Carpathians.
This flat **reminds me strongly of** my grandmother's: the same carpets, the same old clock.
items.watchOut: «Він нагадує мені тата» — He reminds me of my dad: дієслово remind, а не remember, і прийменник of. Remind sb to do sth — нагадати зробити щось: Remind me to buy milk.

items.pattern: vaguely remember sth / doing sth / that…
items.meaning: remember something, but not clearly or in detail
items.example: I **vaguely remember** a red tricycle I had when I was three, but nothing else from that time.
more: I **vaguely remember** meeting him at a wedding years ago.
She **vaguely remembered** reading something about the new bridge in the paper.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /ˈveɪɡli/ — «вейглі», u не читається.

items.pattern: completely / clean forget (about) sth · clean is informal
items.meaning: forget something totally, so it is not in your mind at all
items.example: He'd **completely forgotten** his wife's birthday, so he ran to the florist's before she got home.
more: I was supposed to buy bread on the way home, but I **clean forgot**.
I'd **clean forgotten** that I'd lent you that book years ago.
items.watchOut: Clean тут означає «геть, повністю»: так кажуть розмовно, майже тільки з forget. Якщо називаєш місце, де лишилася річ, кажи leave: I left my keys at work. I forgot my keys at work теж кажуть, але з місцем звичніше leave.

items.pattern: remember sb's face / name · can't remember sb's name
items.meaning: be able to bring back to your mind what someone looks like or what they are called
items.example: I **remember his face** from the gym, but I've no idea what his name is.
more: Do you **remember the name** of that little hotel in Odesa?
I never forget a face, but I can't **remember names** at all.
items.watchOut: «Не пам'ятаю, як її звати» — I can't remember her name або I can't remember what she's called, а не how she is called.

items.pattern: sb's mind goes / went blank
items.meaning: you suddenly can't remember or think of anything
items.uk: усе вилетіло з голови, у голові стало порожньо
items.example: I was about to introduce my two friends to each other, and suddenly my **mind went blank**.
more: At the cash machine my **mind went blank** and I couldn't remember my PIN.
Whenever someone points a camera at me, my **mind goes blank** and I forget how to smile.
items.watchOut: «У голові порожньо» — my mind went blank: зазвичай mind, а не head, і дієслово go, а не became empty.

items.pattern: memories come flooding back (to sb) · it all came flooding back
items.meaning: a lot of memories suddenly return at the same time
items.example: When I tasted that soup in a café in Kraków, the **memories came flooding back**: it was exactly like Mum's.
more: As soon as we drove into the village, it all **came flooding back** to me.
The smell of Grandma's apple pie makes all the **memories come flooding back**.
items.watchOut: Після come — форма з -ing: come flooding back, не come flood back.

items.pattern: sb's earliest memory (is of sth / of doing sth)
items.meaning: the first thing in your life that you can remember
items.example: My **earliest memory** is of a thunderstorm: I was hiding under the kitchen table.
more: What's your **earliest memory**?
Her **earliest memory** of school is crying at the gate on the first day.
items.watchOut: Спогад про щось — a memory of sth, зазвичай з of: my earliest memory of the sea. «Найперший спогад» — найчастіше my earliest memory.

items.pattern: stir up memories (of sth) · stir up old / painful memories
items.meaning: make old memories, often strong or emotional ones, come back
items.example: Watching my son's first football match **stirred up memories** of my own days in the school team.
more: The smell of the sea always **stirs up memories** of my childhood in Odesa.
Selling the family house **stirred up all sorts of memories** for my brothers and me.

items.pattern: distinctly / vividly / clearly remember sth / doing sth / that…
items.meaning: remember something very clearly, as if you can still see or hear it
items.example: I **distinctly remember** telling you about the party. Weren't you listening?
more: She **vividly remembers** her first flight: she was sick the whole way.
Mum **distinctly remembers** the day I was born: it was snowing.
items.watchOut: «Яскраво пам'ятаю» — vividly remember, не brightly: brightly — про світло й кольори. «Чітко пам'ятаю» — distinctly або clearly remember; strongly remember зазвичай не кажуть.

items.pattern: blot out a / the memory (of sth) · blot it out
items.meaning: try hard to stop yourself remembering something unpleasant
items.example: I've tried to **blot out the memory** of my first job interview: I called the manager by the wrong name.
more: After the break-up, he deleted all their photos to **blot out the memories**.
I'd love to **blot out** that whole evening: I said such stupid things.
items.watchOut: Займенник стоїть посередині: blot it out, а не blot out it.

items.pattern: an unforgettable / a memorable experience (trip, day, evening)
items.meaning: something that happened to you that was so special you will always remember it
items.example: Seeing the northern lights in Norway was an **unforgettable experience**.
more: Our first trip to the mountains together was a really **memorable experience**.
Cooking with a real Italian grandmother was a **memorable experience** for the whole class.
items.watchOut: «Незабутні враження» — зазвичай an unforgettable experience (однина); unforgettable impressions звучить як калька: impression — це насамперед думка про когось чи щось. Experience тут — подія, яку пережив, а не «досвід». Артикль: an unforgettable, a memorable.

items.pattern: if I remember rightly / correctly (at the start or end of a sentence)
items.meaning: used when you think a fact is true but you are not completely sure
items.uk: якщо я правильно пам'ятаю, якщо не помиляюся
items.example: **If I remember rightly**, your sister is allergic to nuts, isn't she?
more: We stayed in a small hotel near the station, **if I remember rightly**.
**If I remember correctly**, you owe me a coffee.
items.watchOut: «Якщо пам'ять мене не зраджує» дослівно не перекладай (if my memory doesn't betray me). Кажуть if I remember rightly / correctly або if memory serves (me).

items.pattern: remember sb/sth well · remember it well
items.meaning: remember something clearly and in detail
items.example: I **remember my first teacher well**: she always wore a green scarf.
more: My grandad **remembers the old tram line well**: he took it to school every day.
'Do you know Olena?' 'Yes, I **remember her well** from school.'
items.watchOut: Well стоїть після додатка: I remember it well, а не I remember well it.

items.pattern: memories fade (as time passes / with time) · a fading memory
items.meaning: memories become less clear over time
items.example: Once you stop talking about a place, the **memories fade** surprisingly quickly.
more: Some **memories fade**, but others stay with you for ever.
Luckily, the bad **memories faded** with time.
items.watchOut: «Спогади стираються» — memories fade. Get erased звучить як про техніку чи фантастичне кіно.

items.pattern: painful / unhappy / bad memories (of sth)
items.meaning: memories of something that hurt or upset you
items.example: For my grandmother, the old railway station is full of **painful memories**: it's where she said goodbye to her brother.
more: I have some **painful memories** of being laughed at in PE lessons.
Talking about the divorce still brings back **painful memories** for him.
items.watchOut: «Важкі спогади» — зазвичай painful memories або bad memories. Heavy memories — дослівна калька, так кажуть рідко.

items.pattern: have / get the impression (that)… · I got the impression that…
items.meaning: think that something is true because of what you have seen or heard, though you are not sure
items.example: I **got the impression that** our new neighbours don't like dogs.
more: I **had the impression** that the hotel was closer to the beach. It's miles away!
We **got the impression** that the waiter wanted us to leave.
items.watchOut: «У мене склалося враження» — I got / had the impression, не I made the impression. Make an impression (on sb) — справити враження на когось.

items.pattern: sense (some) tension (between people) · sense the tension in the room
items.meaning: feel, without being told, that people are nervous or angry with each other
items.example: At dinner I **sensed some tension**: my brother and his wife hardly said a word to each other.
more: Our dog always **senses tension** and goes to hide under the bed.
You could **sense the tension** at the airport when the flight was delayed again.
items.watchOut: Напруга між людьми — tension, а не voltage: voltage — це електрична напруга.

items.pattern: have / have got a feeling (that)…
items.meaning: think that something is true or will happen, though you have no proof
items.example: I **have a feeling** it's going to rain, so take an umbrella.
more: I've **got a feeling** we've met before.
She **had a feeling** something was wrong when her son didn't call back.
items.watchOut: З артиклем a: I have a feeling (that)…, не I have feeling. Так кажуть і про передчуття: I have a feeling we'll win.

items.pattern: trust your intuition / instincts
items.meaning: believe that your instinctive feelings are right and act on them
items.example: The road looked fine, but something told me to slow down. I **trusted my intuition**, and there was ice round the corner.
more: When you're choosing a babysitter, **trust your intuition**.
I didn't **trust my intuition**, bought the cheap car and regretted it a week later.
items.watchOut: Trust зазвичай без прийменника: trust your intuition. А rely і depend потребують on: rely on your intuition.

items.pattern: be (ridiculously / a bit) over-sensitive (about sth) · also oversensitive
items.meaning: get upset far too easily, even when nobody meant to hurt you
items.example: He's **ridiculously over-sensitive**: if you don't answer his message within an hour, he thinks you're angry with him.
more: My brother is **over-sensitive** about his height, so don't mention it.
Teenagers can be **over-sensitive** about their looks.
items.watchOut: Over- означає «занадто», тож over-sensitive — завжди критика. Пишуть і разом: oversensitive.

items.pattern: be sensitive to heat / light / cold / noise
items.meaning: react badly or very easily to heat, light, etc.
items.example: Grandma is very **sensitive to heat**, so we visit her at the seaside in May, not August.
more: Some medicines make your skin **sensitive to light**, so stay in the shade.
Our cat is very **sensitive to noise** and hides when we hoover.
items.watchOut: Прийменник to: sensitive to light, to cold, to noise — не on і не for.

items.pattern: sensitive skin / teeth / eyes · have sensitive skin
items.meaning: skin or teeth that react easily and are easily hurt or irritated
items.example: My **sensitive skin** goes red if I use cheap washing powder.
more: Ice cream hurts because I have **sensitive teeth**.
Wool makes me itch: I've always had **sensitive skin**.
items.watchOut: Чутлива шкіра — sensitive skin, а не sensible skin: sensible — «розсудливий», це хибний друг. І шкіра людини — skin, а leather — шкіра як матеріал (сумка, куртка).

items.pattern: go numb (with cold) · be numb · numb fingers
items.meaning: lose all feeling in a part of your body, for example from cold
items.example: After an hour waiting for the bus in the frost, my feet had **gone numb**.
more: My arm **went numb** because the baby had been sleeping on it all night.
The dentist's injection made half my face **go numb**.
items.watchOut: b у кінці не вимовляється: /nʌm/. «Пальці заніміли» — my fingers went numb: дієслово go, не did numb і не made numb.

items.phrase: acute hearing / an acute sense of smell
items.pattern: acute hearing · an acute sense of smell / taste
items.meaning: a very good, sharp ability to hear or smell
items.example: My mum has an **acute sense of smell**: she knows if anyone has smoked in the car, even a week later.
more: Cats have **acute hearing** and can hear a mouse under the floor.
Some people with poor eyesight develop very **acute hearing**.
items.watchOut: «Гострий нюх» — an acute sense of smell: потрібне слово sense. Про сам запах «різкий» кажуть a sharp / strong smell, а не acute. Вимова: /əˈkjuːt/, наголос на другому складі.

items.pattern: a (very) sensitive person / child · be sensitive
items.meaning: someone who is easily upset or hurt by what other people say or do
items.example: Be careful what you say about his drawing. He's **a very sensitive child**.
more: My aunt is **a sensitive person** and cries at every sad film.
She's very **sensitive**, so tell her the bad news gently.
items.watchOut: Не плутай: a sensitive person — вразлива людина, a sensible person — розсудлива.

items.pattern: a (very) sensible person · be sensible · the sensible thing to do
items.meaning: someone with good judgement who does practical, reasonable things
items.example: My grandfather was **a very sensible person**: he never bought anything he couldn't pay for.
more: Wearing a helmet is the **sensible** thing to do.
Be **sensible** and take a taxi home: it's too late to walk.
items.watchOut: Хибний друг: sensible — не «чутливий», а «розсудливий, розважливий». Чутлива, вразлива людина — sensitive.

warmup.uk: Ця пісня дуже нагадує мені про літо в бабусі.
warmup.q: This song ___ me strongly of summers at my gran's.
warmup.explain: Нагадувати комусь про щось — remind sb of sth. Remember і recall — пам'ятати, згадувати самому.

warmup.uk: Я чітко пам'ятаю, що замикав двері.
warmup.explain: Чітко пам'ятаю — distinctly (або clearly) remember. Strongly remember зазвичай не кажуть, brightly — про світло.

warmup.uk: Я так хвилювався, що все вилетіло з голови.
warmup.q: I was so nervous that my mind went ___.
warmup.explain: У голові порожньо — my mind went blank.
Незабутні враження — an unforgettable experience. Impression — думка про когось чи щось, а не пережита подія.

warmup.uk: У мене склалося враження, що вона втомилася.
warmup.q: I ___ the impression that she was tired.
warmup.explain: Склалося враження — I got / had the impression. Make an impression — справити враження на когось.

warmup.uk: У мене від холоду заніміли пальці.
warmup.explain: Заніміти — go numb: my fingers went numb.
Trust your intuition — без прийменника. Rely і depend потребують on: rely on your intuition.
Чутлива шкіра — sensitive skin. Sensible — розсудливий, це хибний друг.

A.q: I can't remember the name of that film at all. Give me a ___.
A.explain: Дай підказку — give me a clue (або a hint). Sign — знак, key — ключ, вони тут не підходять.

A.q: I'd ___ forgotten about the party until Anna phoned to ask where I was.
A.explain: Геть забути — completely forget (розмовно: clean forget). Strongly з forget не вживають, а vaguely — «невиразно» — кажуть про remember.

A.q: It's been fifteen years since I left school, and my memories of my classmates are starting to ___.

B.q: After the interview, I ___ the impression that they'd already chosen someone else.
B.explain: У мене склалося враження — I got / had the impression. Make an impression — справити враження на інших.

B.q: Musicians often have ___ hearing and notice even a tiny mistake.
B.explain: Гострий слух — acute (або sharp, keen) hearing.

B.q: You can lend Petro your car. He's a very ___ driver and never takes risks.
B.explain: Sensible — розсудливий. Sensitive — вразливий, чутливий; sentimental — сентиментальний.

example.title: The old photo album
example.uk:
Минулих вихідних я допомагав мамі розбирати горище, і ми знайшли старий фотоальбом. Коли я гортав сторінки, нахлинули спогади. Мій найперший спогад — маленький садок за нашою першою квартирою, і ось він був на фото, а в ньому я в жовтому капелюшку.

На одному знімку була дівчинка, яка дуже нагадувала мені мою доньку. Її обличчя я пам'ятав ще з дитсадка, а от ім'я геть забув. «Дай підказку», — попросив я. «Вона жила по сусідству, — відповіла мама. — Катя, якщо я правильно пам'ятаю».

І раптом я яскраво згадав, як ми з нею ліпили сніговика, аж поки в нас не заніміли пальці. Сумно, що спогади блякнуть, але деяким із них просто треба трохи допомогти.
example.en:
Last weekend I helped Mum clear out the attic, and we found an old photo album. As I turned the pages, the [[memories came flooding back|a10]]. My [[earliest memory|a11]] is of the little garden behind our first flat, and there it was, with me in a yellow hat.

One photo showed a girl who [[reminded me strongly of|a5]] my daughter. I [[remembered her face|a8]] from my nursery days, but her name? I'd [[completely forgotten|a7]] it. '[[Give me a clue|a4]],' I said. 'She lived next door,' Mum answered. 'Katya, [[if I remember rightly|a16]].'

Suddenly I could [[vividly remember|a13]] the two of us building a snowman until our fingers [[went numb|b8]]. It's sad how [[memories fade|a18]], but some of them just need a little help.
